** Minor** · **Maintainability & Code Quality** · **Quick win** **Use the orchestrator as the claim owner.** Line 137 declares `mac/orch-opus` as active, but this row assigns LOT-080 to `mac/w1-080-opus`. The `AGENTS.md` rule requires the active orchestrator to claim lots that it hands out. Set the owner to the orchestrator, or document why this lot is not being handed out by the active orchestrator, before keeping status `in-progress`. As per path instructions, `docs/**` must stay consistent with `AGENTS.md`; the applicable rule says, “when an orchestrator is active, it claims instead.”

review_comments.body:
@francoisgn You are correct. I confused the session that makes the claim with the session recorded as owner. The quoted Claims rule permits the orchestrator to claim on behalf of its child session. `mac/w1-080-opus` is consistent with that rule and the other Wave 1 rows. No change is needed. I withdraw this finding. ---

An orchestrator can make one claim PR for the lots it hands out, record each child session's ID as owner, and pass the same ID to that child. Do not require the orchestrator's own ID in the Owner column merely because the orchestrator makes the claim. ``` > Note: Learnings are effective only in the context of similar code segments.
